name: two_shaft_gas_turbine_compressor_map
title: Two-shaft gas turbine with a compressor map and two expanders
summary: Steady-state model of a two-shaft gas turbine (single-spool compressor and combustor, two mechanically independent expanders) on air: the compressor is described by a performance map (reduced flow, pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency versus reduced speed), the combustor by an energy balance with the mean specific heats of the ULiege combustion library, and expander 1 by a power balance from which its isentropic efficiency is found. Revision exercise of the ULiege course 'Machines et systemes thermiques', in three parts.
language_features: INTERPOLATE (native EES call form with a named argument)
$INCLUDE cpbar_combustion_products (CSL-0005) for the user-library routines cpbar and gamma (copied in the runnable variants); cpbar called with CALL

origin.course: MECA0006 Machines et systèmes thermiques (ULiège), revision exercises of 2005-12-23, part 2

verification.summary: Compared with the EES stored solutions of the three revision files (TM-0150, TM-0151, TM-0149): max relative deviation 1.6·10⁻³ (mean cp of air), derived results within 1.1·10⁻³ (EES vs CoolProp air); h_1, h_2, h_2s, s_1 differ by the air reference state. The main file, with $INCLUDE cpbar_combustion_products (CSL-0005) and CALL cpbar, equals its _coolsolve variant.
verification.reference: EES stored solutions of the three files of the revision exercise: TM-0150 (main file, nominal speed), TM-0151 (ambient variant, 0.76 bar and 0 °C) and TM-0149 (95 % speed, t_ex_burner and epsilon_s_exp1 given), compared with tools/compare_solution.py
verification.notes: 40 of the 44 EES variables agree within 1.6e-3 relative (largest: the mean specific heat of air, 1.6e-3); all derived results (powers, temperatures, efficiency, flows) within 1.1e-3. h_1, h_2, h_2s and s_1 differ by CoolProp's reference state for air; their differences agree to 6e-4. Same deviations for the ambient variant (max 1.4e-3) and for the 95 % speed case. Re-solved with CoolSolve 0.3.0@4798e2b: the variants now use the native INTERPOLATE call form (named argument), solutions unchanged. Concerns the variants until 2026-11-04; then the main file runs with $INCLUDE cpbar_combustion_products and its two cpbar calls in CALL form (workflow §3), from the variant's .initials, and equals the _coolsolve variant on all 52 common variables; vs TM-0150 it prints '44 common variables, 7 differ (rtol=0.001)', as the variant (CoolSolve 0.4.0@2f4860b).
